root_cause.text: The `bcmgenet_put_txcb` function was calculating the tx_cb pointer before rewinding the write_ptr, causing it to return the wrong (next) tx_cb instead of the one that should be cleaned up.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the pointer calculation (`tx_cb_ptr = ring->cbs; tx_cb_ptr += ring->write_ptr - ring->cb_ptr;`) to occur **after** the write_ptr rewind logic. The commit message explicitly states: "The write_ptr points to the next open tx_cb. We want to return the tx_cb that gets rewinded, so we must rewind the pointer first then return the tx_cb that it points to." This off-by-one error meant the function was returning an incorrect tx_cb, preventing proper cleanup of transmission control blocks.

The new `bcmgenet_put_txcb()` function (lines 1205-1220) correctly handles the tx_cb pointer calculation by FIRST rewinding the write_ptr (lines 1213-1216) BEFORE calculating the tx_cb_ptr (lines 1208-1209). The old vulnerable code in `bcmgenet_xmit_single()` and `bcmgenet_xmit_frag()` (which calculated tx_cb before rewinding) has been removed and consolidated into the main `bcmgenet_xmit()` function with proper error handling using the new `bcmgenet_put_txcb()` helper.
